widgets_values:
Base scheduler steps = total steps. The split-sigmas value = Pass 1 steps (min 6); total minus that = Pass 2 steps (min 4).
E.g. total 12, sigmas 8 → Pass 1 = 8, Pass 2 = 4. Total 10, sigmas 6 → Pass 1 = 6, Pass 2 = 4.

Tip: Pass 1 needs 6+ steps — use 8 for better audio quality.
Mixed-input cap: images + videos + audio combined must total 12 or fewer!
Up to 9 reference images max. Mute (bypass) any LoadImage node you're not using.

Up to 3 audio refs (must pair with an image or video, 15s total max) — sets pace, dialogue, or ambience.
Up to 3 video refs (2-15s each, 15s total max) — defines camera movement or motion.

The megapixels in the Resolution Examples table are reference values for the Resolution Selector above, not for the Pass 2 scale — you calculate that yourself.
E.g. Pass 1 at 0.5MP (960x544) with a 1.5x Pass 2 scale = 1440x816 output. A 2x scale = 1920x1088.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - her face, hair and outfit follow <Picture 1> exactly, with no change of clothing, hairstyle, accessories or expression.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, widescreen 16:9 framing, one continuous unbroken shot with no cuts. The camera is <Subject 1>'s own phone, held in her raised hand at arm's length in front of her and slightly above eye level, framing her from the chest up, held slightly left of centre so the street opens out behind her right shoulder. The framing, arm position and angle stay the same throughout - the phone never lowers, never swings away and never pulls back - and the image carries the small continuous handheld sway and step-bounce of someone walking while filming. She is walking along a busy city street in the late afternoon: shopfronts and awnings sliding past behind her, parked cars at the kerb, and a steady flow of other pedestrians moving past her and away down the pavement, all well out of focus. Low sun comes in from one side. She looks straight into the lens while she talks. Her expression stays exactly as it is in <Picture 1>, with no invented expression change. She speaks at a brisk, natural, continuous pace. The young woman (S1) says: <d>[English] Okay, so I am out on the street now.</d> At 00:02.500 she says: <d>[English] I am walking, the camera is moving, people are going past me.</d> She keeps walking and looking into the lens until the video ends.

overall_soundscape:
Open city street ambience: traffic at a distance, footsteps and voices of other people blurred into the background. Closer in, her own footsteps, the rustle of her clothing, and light outdoor air on a phone microphone.

ULTRA SPEED - Singularity 4-step
=====================================

WHAT CHANGED FROM THE BEST WORKFLOW
  Model  -> Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v1.3_int8
  LoRA   -> minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1
  Sampling -> the Dual Clock node drives it, single pass
  The whole second pass is still here, just bypassed (purple nodes)

  NOTE: Singularity only works with the 4step v0.1 LoRA.
  Do not swap in the 8step one.

SETTING THE STEP COUNT  (this is the only knob - leave resolution at 1.0MP)
  Green Dual Clock node, first field: steps. You never touch a sigma string.

    6 steps   THE DEFAULT. Low-motion shots: talking to camera, walking,
              slow moves. This is the sweet spot of the whole workflow.
    8 steps   High motion: dancing, arms swinging freely, crowds.
    4 steps   Works, but with no margin. It drops words out of spoken
              dialogue when the line is clipped or has weak syllables:
              'Four. Not forty. Four.' lost its 'not' every single time,
              while 'Not forty steps, not twelve - just four.' came out
              clean. Only use 4 if speed matters more than the voice.

  KEEP RESOLUTION AT 1.0MP (1360x768 / 768x1360). That is the LoRA's
  native 768p scale, and what a normal GPU can actually run. Steps buy
  more than pixels: 4 steps at 1.4MP (243s) looked WORSE than 6 steps at
  1.0MP (206s). Spend on steps, not on resolution.

  Timings, a 10s clip at 1.0MP:  4 steps 153s | 6 steps 206s
  Motion is free - a big-motion dance took 205s, the same as a
  locked-off talking head. Only frames x pixels cost anything.

  The sigma curve is NOT a lever. DualClock/beta, DualClock/native_flow
  and a hand-written turbo curve all rendered in ~242s and looked the
  same. Don't waste time there - step count is what moves quality.

WHAT BREAKS AND WHEN
  Ask one question: how much SMALL, FAST-MOVING detail is in frame?

   fine at 4    talking to camera, sitting, walking, slow moves,
                plain or shallow-focus background
   fine at 4    hands resting on knees, gripping a pole, holding a cup -
                anything with a contact point
   needs 6-8    both arms swinging freely in the air
   needs 6-8    busy backgrounds - crowds, traffic, rain, leaves.
                Background pedestrians ghost as they walk away.
   don't bother inversions, flips, dunks - more steps won't fix these

IF THE AUDIO SOUNDS THIN
  Change shift_audio on the Dual Clock node (default 3).
  Do NOT add steps - 4 steps and 8 steps sound identical, the step
  count is not an audio control.
  Audio quality tracks clip length and how much dialogue you write:
  a short clip with one line will always sound hollow.
  Write one line every 2.5s - two lines in a 5s clip, six in a 15s one.

RESOLUTION
  1.0MP is already publishable (768x1360). A 5s talking-head clip
  renders in 76s, a 15s one in 262s.
  The LoRA was trained at 768p,

TURNING THE SECOND PASS BACK ON
  You can (select the purple nodes, press Ctrl+B), but know what it
  gives you: a BIGGER picture, not a SHARPER one. Detail only ever
  carries the resolution it was generated at; upscaling cannot invent
  what was never there.
  Want it sharper? Raise megapixels on the ResolutionSelector instead.
